exact_statement: Let a=2/ln2. On any restriction-closed class of uniform Boolean signs, B<=lambda H+K I with 0<=lambda<1,K>=0 implies H<=(K+a)/(1-lambda) I. If every Boolean f with max_i Inf_i<tau in (0,1) has a relevant i satisfying B_i<=(lambda H/I+K)Inf_i, then FEI holds at C=max(log2(e/tau)+a,(K+a)/(1-lambda)). Requiring i in G_c={i:Inf_i>=c I/d}, d=#relevant inputs,c in (0,1), leaves the forward constant unchanged; FEI(C) implies this restricted selection with lambda=0,K=C/(1-c). More generally B_G<=lambda H+KI in the weak regime with 0<=lambda<1-c implies C=max(log2(e/tau)+a,(K+a(1-c))/(1-c-lambda)). The fixed open rule c=1/2,tau=1/4,lambda=0,K=4 would imply FEI(4+2/ln2), but that rule itself is not proved.

exact_statement: For every even k>=4 let f_k be canonical B05 with k quadratic-bent data bits,2k point-activation controls and retained selector y. Replace all 3k background inputs by disjoint Majority_M blocks with M=2^(2k+3)+1, obtaining an actual Boolean F_k on D=3kM+1 bits. Set delta=2^-k,p=delta^2. Its selector is the unique maximum-influence input with Inf_y=pdelta, every background influence is <pdelta/2, and B_y(F_k)/Inf_y(F_k)=B_y(f_k)/(pdelta)>=(1-delta)(k-2)->infinity. Both max influence and total influence tend to zero. Thus no finite fixed K pays B_i<=K Inf_i at a maximum-influence coordinate for all weak-influence Boolean signs. The same no-go holds for entropy decrement Delta_i. Nevertheless every background input satisfies Inf_i>=I(F_k)/(2D) and B_i/Inf_i<1, so this family does not refute the high-average-cutoff rule. The proof uses exact balanced-block retained-coordinate B,Delta,JS invariance and the odd-Majority internal-edge formula sum_T Phi(p_T,rho^2 p_(T+j)).
